data.claim: A landing whose changed paths overlap another merged item's changed paths is recorded as merge.reconciled {files,base,main}, and ddflow complete is then refused until tests pass on the reconciled tree unless [lease].reconcile_tests=off; the default is 'affected' (D-gate-economy-r3), strictest 'full'.
data.falsifier: A complete that records a non-empty merge.reconciled yet succeeds with no passed unit_tests/ci on the reconciled tree refutes the guard.
data.mechanism: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py records merge.reconciled from the file intersection of this item's committed changes vs every other item merged since its fork; ddflow/services/completion/rules.py _reconciled_blocker appends a blocker when reconciled.files is non-empty and neither unit_tests (nor ci for 'affected') has passed.
data.question: Does merging files another item changed since this one forked need a reconcile-and-test guard before complete?

chunk_findings.detail: When `it.base_sha` is empty the fork falls back to `landed_before`, which already contains every item merged onto main before this landing. `GIT.is_ancestor(other.merged_sha, fork) is not False` is then true for those items, so they are skipped and `merge.reconciled` is never appended. Given two items that both edit `foo.py`, the first already merged, and the second has no `base_sha`, complete is not refused. The same `is not False` also treats an unknown ancestry result (`None`) as "already merged before the fork" and drops the overlap, so the safety net fails open.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_record_reconciled

chunk_findings.detail: The required trigger is file overlap with an item merged since the base **or** a main-into-branch conflict, and `Item.reconciled` documents the conflict case, but this writer only intersects `changed_paths` of other items. A landing that conflicts with main (direct commit, or an item with no `merged_sha` / empty `landed_before`..`landed_after`) and is resolved without that intersection records nothing, so complete proceeds with no reconciled-tree test evidence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_record_reconciled

chunk_findings.detail: A passed `unit_tests` or `ci` gate recorded at any time, with any evidence, clears the reconcile guard. Given `merge.reconciled` files `["src/x.py"]` and `[lease].reconcile_tests = "affected"` (the new default), if `gate_outcome("ci")` is already `PASSED` from a run before the reconcile — or with evidence `"selected tests"` that never names `src/x.py` or the reconciled base/main — the function returns `""` at the `if passed` check and `verdict` does not block complete. The mandatory net is that affected tests passed on the reconciled tree, with evidence naming those files and that run; this accepts a stale or unrelated pass. `test_a_reconciled_merge_with_a_passed_ci_completes` locks that bypass in.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:_reconciled_blocker

chunk_findings.detail: In `_record_reconciled`, the loop iterates over `st.items.items()` and calls `GIT.is_ancestor(repo, other.merged_sha, fork)`, but `other` is an `Item` model object whose `merged_sha` attribute may not exist or may be named differently in the item model (e.g., `landed_after` or stored via event data). Given an item `other` where `other.merged_sha` returns an empty string or AttributeError/TypeError inside `is_ancestor` (since `merged_sha` is not a field on `Item`), the merge lifecycle crashes with an attribute error when completing any merge, preventing all item completions.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:112

chunk_findings.detail: The safety net only records `merge.reconciled` for path overlap with another item’s `landed_before..landed_after`. A main-into-branch conflict is never consulted, despite the field docs and the decision this change claims to implement. Given item A edits only `F`, main gains an edit to `F` that is not another item’s landed range (direct commit, or an item with empty `landed_before`/`landed_after`), the merge conflicts and is resolved: `_record_reconciled` leaves `files` empty, appends nothing, and complete is not refused on the reconciled tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_record_reconciled

chunk_findings.detail: `_reconciled_blocker` treats any existing `unit_tests` PASSED (and, unless `reconcile_tests == "full"`, any `ci` PASSED) as proof the reconciled tree was tested. `gate_outcome` is not compared to `merge.reconciled` or to `reconciled["main"]`, and the evidence string is never required to name the reconciled files. Given T1 already has `unit_tests` (or `ci`) PASSED from the pre-merge run, then `merge.reconciled` is recorded for `src/x.py` because another item changed that file since the fork, `passed` is already true and the function returns `""`, so `verdict` allows complete without a run on the reconciled tree. That is the case the guard exists to refuse (D-lease-hold-limit-r2).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:297

chunk_findings.detail: The empty-`base_sha` half of the earlier finding is still live. The a9c818f13 change only tightened the skip from `is not False` to `is True`; `fork = it.base_sha or landed_before` is unchanged. Given two items that both edit `foo.py`, the first already merged onto main, and the second landing with `it.base_sha == ""`, `fork` is `landed_before`, which already contains that first item's `merged_sha`. `GIT.is_ancestor(repo, other.merged_sha, fork) is True`, so the other item is skipped, `files` stays empty, and `merge.reconciled` is never appended. Complete is therefore not refused. A `None` ancestry result no longer drops the overlap; a missing base still does.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_record_reconciled

chunk_findings.detail: The timestamp check does not close the evidence half of the prior blocker. Given `merge.reconciled` `{"files": ["src/x.py"], "at": "2026-10-17T12:00:00", "base": "aaa", "main": "bbb"}` and `[lease].reconcile_tests = "affected"`, a `ci` (or `unit_tests`) record with `outcome == PASSED`, `at` equal to or after that stamp, and evidence `"selected tests"` that never names `src/x.py` or the reconciled base/main still makes `passed_on_reconciled_tree` true, so the function returns `""` and complete is not refused. Nothing in this guard requires the pass to be the affected suite for those files.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:_reconciled_blocker

chunk_findings.detail: A missing reconcile timestamp fails open. `reconciled_at = it.reconciled.get("at") or ""`, and any non-empty `rec.at >= ""` is true. Given `reconciled = {"files": ["src/x.py"]}` (no `at`) and a pre-merge `unit_tests` PASSED at `"2020-01-01T00:00:00"`, the guard clears and complete proceeds with no run on the reconciled tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:_reconciled_blocker

chunk_findings.detail: The a9c818f13 fix only requires a `ci`/`unit_tests` pass at-or-after `merge.reconciled`; it does not require evidence that names the reconciled files, and this new test locks that hole in. Given `merge.reconciled` files `["src/x.py"]` and the default `lease.reconcile_tests=affected`, `test_a_reconciled_merge_with_a_passed_ci_completes` records `gate record T1 ci --outcome passed --evidence "selected tests"` and asserts the reconcile blocker is gone. That evidence names neither `src/x.py` nor the reconciled base/main, so a post-reconcile gate for some other selection clears complete. The governing note only replaces the full suite with affected tests; it does not drop the required evidence naming the reconciled files and the suite run.

chunk_findings.detail: In `_record_reconciled`, the loop iterates over `st.items.items()` to compare other items' `merged_sha` against `fork`. However, `Item` objects do not have a `merged_sha` attribute (they store merge information via worktree events or `landed_after`), raising an `AttributeError` whenever a merge occurs and breaking the completion of merges.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:108

chunk_findings.detail: Overlap is taken against every other item with a `merged_sha` that is not an ancestor of this item's fork, with no check that that sha is in the main being landed (`landed_before` / `landed_after`). Given item A forked from main at F, item B merged only onto a side branch at S (S not an ancestor of F) and both touched `src/x.py`, A's clean merge to main still appends `merge.reconciled` and complete is refused, even though B's edits are not in this landing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_record_reconciled

chunk_findings.detail: The required conflict case is never recorded. The function returns immediately when `changed_paths(fork, tip=branch_head)` is empty, and otherwise only intersects that pre-merge branch diff with other items' `landed_before..landed_after` ranges. A main-into-branch conflict on `foo.py` against a direct main hotfix (no item `merged_sha` covering that commit), or a resolution that exists only in the merge commit, lands with no `merge.reconciled` event, so complete is not held for tests on the reconciled tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_record_reconciled

chunk_findings.detail: `_record_reconciled` only appends `merge.reconciled` when this branch's committed paths intersect another item's `landed_before..landed_after` range. A main-into-branch merge that conflicts, but whose conflicting main commits are not another item's landed range (direct commit, or an item skipped because `removed` / missing `merged_sha`), never records the event. Example: base `B0`, main then gains `foo` from a non-item commit, the branch edits `foo` and the merge conflicts and is resolved; `mine ∩ theirs` is empty, so no `merge.reconciled` is written and complete is not held for a reconciled-tree test run. The governing note still requires that conflict case (it only overrides the suite default to `affected`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:98

chunk_findings.detail: `passed_on_reconciled_tree` treats any later `unit_tests` `PASSED` record as proof the reconciled tree was tested. Given `reconcile_tests="affected"` (the default), `it.reconciled={"files":["ddflow/foo.py"],"at":"2026-10-17T12:00:00Z","base":"abc","main":"def"}` and a `unit_tests` gate with `outcome=PASSED`, `at` equal to that stamp, and evidence that does not name `ddflow/foo.py` (or names a different tree), line 310 returns true and `_reconciled_blocker` returns `""`, so complete is allowed. That violates the required gate: affected tests must have passed on the reconciled tree, with evidence naming the reconciled files. A timestamp compare never checks the tree, the file set, or the evidence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:310

chunk_findings.detail: When `reconcile_tests` is not `"full"`, a post-reconcile `ci` pass clears the blocker even if `unit_tests` failed or never ran. Given the default `"affected"`, reconciled files present, `unit_tests` `FAILED` after `reconciled.at`, and `ci` `PASSED` after `reconciled.at` (docs/lint only), line 314 sets `passed` true and complete is not refused. The message on the failure path only cites `unit_tests`, so `ci` is not the affected-test evidence the note requires.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:314

chunk_findings.detail: The regression this task requires (two branches edit the same file, the second merges, complete stays refused until suite evidence is on the reconciled tree) is never run. `_reconciled` appends `merge.reconciled` itself, and the manifest’s only new tests are in this file. A merge path that never records reconciliation, never detects overlap, and never conflicts still leaves every test here green, including `test_a_reconciled_merge_folds_onto_the_item_and_refuses_complete`.
